items.title: The wallet balance chart and the admin trend and daily charts can now be read with the keyboard
items.where_users_meet_it: 1) Board (signed-in home page /): on a pilot's sheet, the Wallet card's 'Wallet balance over time' line chart. It only appears when that pilot has no net-worth figure yet: the assets scope was not granted, or the first net-worth value has not been recorded. Otherwise the Wallet card shows the net-worth chart instead. 2) Admin console: /admin (Audience card, page views per day); /admin/traffic (Activity, page views per day with a 7-day average); /admin/health (price cron 'Rows fetched by day', service-level 'Failures by day'); /admin/search (each '... by day' chart, plus Index coverage 'Indexed' and 'Not indexed'); /admin/esi ('Scheduled Fuzzwork share by day'). 3) /preview/primitives: the TrendChart and AnnotatedDailyChart specimens, including the 'one day of data' variant. Not affected: the bar charts, such as /admin/esi 'Degradation events by caller' and the BarChart specimen. They stay mouse-only.
items.before: These charts worked only with a mouse or touch. Hovering or tapping showed a small tooltip with the value and date, plus a dashed vertical line with a dot on the line or bar. The keyboard could not reach them: Tab went straight past every one. A screen reader heard only the chart's name as a picture, for example 'Wallet balance over time'. The board's net-worth chart could already be read with the keyboard; these charts could not.
items.after: Each of these charts is now a Tab stop and works like the net-worth chart. When you Tab onto a chart, three things happen. A thin muted-green rounded outline appears around it. The dashed line and dot jump to the most recent point. The tooltip shows that point, for example '1.23B · 9 Oct 2026' on the balance chart or '412 · 2026-10-11 · 7d avg 380' on a page-views chart. The Left and Right arrow keys step one point back or forward and stop at the first and last points, with no wrap-around. Up, Down, Home and End do nothing. Tabbing away or clicking elsewhere hides the tooltip. Screen readers now announce '<chart name>; use the arrow keys to read each day', but they do not read out the values you step to, because the tooltip is hidden from assistive tech. The net-worth chart already had this gap, and Greptile logged it as a follow-up. Mouse users see no difference: hover works as before, and clicking a chart shows no outline and does not move the tooltip (see 3a8e28c3). Small side effects: after clicking a chart, the arrow keys step from the point you were hovering. Keyboard users on admin pages also get one more Tab stop per chart, which adds up on /admin/search. On the wallet balance chart, one arrow press is one journal sample (up to 48 across about 30 days), so the same date can show on two presses in a row despite the 'each day' wording. Hover already did this. At rest the charts look the same as before: same axes, up to five date labels under the plot with the first and last tucked inward, whole-number value gridlines, and the same colours, sizes, tooltip text and tooltip placement.
items.behind_the_scenes: TrendChart and AnnotatedDailyChart are now built on the shared TimeSeriesFrame. That is the shell the net-worth chart already used: focus outline and arrow keys, canvas and tooltip, date labels, crosshair and hover area. The old chart/line-chart.tsx is deleted, along with the daily chart's hand-built date axis and hover layer. A small ChartBaseline draws the bottom edge line, and all five chart types share default number and label formatters. Unused options (className, xTicks), the tickIndices re-export, SparklinePoint and the daily model's xs were removed.
items.risk_notes: Low. Tests check that the at-rest output matches: tick positions, tick labels, layer order, the tab stop and both labels. The wallet balance chart cannot be shown locally. The E2E Pilot has no ESI data, and every demo-board pilot has a net-worth figure, so they all show the net-worth chart instead. The primitives page renders the same TrendChart component and stands in for it. The admin Activity chart needs at least one local page view, so browse a couple of pages first. The other admin charts depend on cron, Search Console or ESI data that a local stack probably lacks. Accessibility: the label sits on a plain focusable div with no role, so some screen readers may not speak it, and stepped values are silent. Both gaps already exist on the net-worth chart and are logged as follow-ups, not fixed in this promote.

items.title: Clicking or tapping a chart keeps the day you pointed at, and the arrow-key position survives the board's 30-second refresh
items.where_users_meet_it: Net-worth charts on the board: the Overview 'Wealth' card and each pilot's Wallet card ('Estimated net worth over time'), on the signed-in home page / and on the demo board at /?demo. Also the StackedAreaChart and SplitAxisChart samples on /preview/primitives. The same rule covers every chart that P004 makes focusable (wallet balance, admin trend and daily charts).
items.before: On staging the net-worth chart already had a Tab stop, but it treated any focus, including a mouse click or a finger tap, as a keyboard Tab. On desktop, if you hovered a day two months back and clicked, the tooltip and dot jumped to today's value at the right-hand end while the pointer was still on the older day. They stayed there until the mouse moved. On phones (Android Chrome and similar), the first tap on the chart read out the newest day instead of the tapped one; only a second tap showed the tapped day. The signed-in board also refreshes its clock every 30 seconds. A keyboard user who had arrowed back ten days lost their place at that refresh, and the next arrow press restarted from the newest day.
items.after: Only keyboard focus (Tab or Shift+Tab) jumps the readout to the newest day and shows the outline. A click or tap keeps the day under the pointer, so the first tap on a phone reads the day you tapped. The arrow keys carry on from the day currently shown, even after the 30-second refresh. For the wallet balance and admin charts that P004 makes focusable, mouse and touch behave exactly as they do on staging today. Without this fix they would have picked up the same jump.
items.behind_the_scenes: The chart's focus handler in chart-frame.tsx seeds the last point only when the browser reports keyboard-style focus (:focus-visible). The arrow-key handler finds the shown point by its x value rather than by object identity, so a parent that rebuilds its data on every render no longer resets it. The same commit's system-index change belongs to the structure composer and is outside this chart area.
items.risk_notes: Low. The fix relies on the browsers' :focus-visible rules: focusing a div by mouse or touch does not count as focus-visible. This was checked in Chromium only; Safari and Firefox follow the same rule. Programmatic focus (as in tests) may not jump to the last day, but the arrow keys still start from the end. The 30-second refresh fix cannot be screenshotted locally. It needs a signed-in board with net-worth history, the E2E Pilot has no ESI data, and the /?demo board renders once and does not refresh. Unit tests cover both halves. The touch shot depends on Playwright's tap emulation firing the browser's usual mouse events. If neither ref shows a tooltip after the tap, drop that shot.

items.title: Both net-worth chart modes draw their bands with one shared piece
items.where_users_meet_it: The board's net-worth charts (Overview 'Wealth' card and each pilot's Wallet card) in both modes. Stacked mode shows ISK with assets on top. Split mode shows net worth above a dashed break and ISK below it. It also covers the StackedAreaChart and SplitAxisChart samples on /preview/primitives.
items.before: Each mode had its own copy of the band drawing: a filled area, a line along its top, and a 3px dot for a lone point with no neighbours, so a band that has just started still shows. In stacked mode, a value left out entirely was drawn at zero height by the area and line, while the dot logic treated it as missing.
items.after: It looks and behaves the same. Both modes keep the same margins, so the plot does not shift when a pilot's chart switches mode. Opacities, line widths, colours and dots are unchanged. A value left out entirely is now a gap everywhere, the same as a value marked 'no data'. No current chart sends a left-out value: the net-worth chart always sends both ISK and assets, and a missing asset value arrives as an explicit 'no data', which was already a gap. So nothing visible changes. Days when the account never opened the board still join up as before, and days with no asset value still break the assets band as before.
items.behind_the_scenes: A new BandSeries component and a shared BAND_CHART_MARGIN in ui/chart/band-series.tsx replace the duplicated area, line and lone-point dot code in StackedAreaChart and SplitAxisChart.
items.risk_notes: Low. Tests compare the markup: missing values and 'no data' render the same, lone points get their dots, and the margins are unchanged. No screenshot is planned because there is nothing to see. For a sanity check, the Wealth chart on /?demo should look identical on both refs.

items.title: Board charts where every value is zero now span -1 to 1 ISK
items.where_users_meet_it: Board (signed-in home page /): the Wallet card's 'Wallet balance over time' chart, and the ISK segment (the lower part) of the split-axis net-worth chart on a pilot's Wallet card or on the Overview Wealth card.
items.before: When every value in the series was exactly zero, the chart padded its range by a tenth of an ISK. The wallet balance chart showed a flat line in the middle with a single gridline, '0.00'. In the split net-worth chart, the ISK segment showed a flat blue line in the middle of the lower band, labelled '-0.10', '0.00', '0.10'. The likeliest real case is the second one: an alt that has held 0 ISK the whole time but owns assets. That puts its chart in split mode with an all-zero ISK band.
items.after: The range is padded by 1 ISK instead. The wallet balance chart still shows a flat line in the middle, now with three gridlines: '-1.00', '0.00', '1.00'. The split chart's ISK segment is labelled '-1.00', '0.00', '1.00', and the line stays in the same place. Any series that is not all zeros (rising, falling, flat at a non-zero value, or negative) gets exactly the same range as before.
items.behind_the_scenes: The board's private fittedDomain is replaced by the shared paddedDomain. The same commit exports readyData and uses it in place of five inline 'is this section ready' checks, and it exports the journal, attributes and implants data types from the board API contract. Those parts have no visible effect.
items.risk_notes: Very low, and rare: an all-zero wallet balance chart practically never happens, and the zero-ISK alt is the realistic case. It cannot be shown with local data. The demo pilots all hold positive ISK, the E2E Pilot has no ESI data, and no preview specimen has an all-zero series, so no shot is planned. It could be staged by intercepting GET /api/account/board, as e2e/home-board.spec.ts does, with a pilot whose wallet is 0 ISK on every history day and whose assets are above 0. Negative ISK labels on a zero-ISK band look a little odd both before and after. If that bothers you, the follow-up would be to keep the ISK band from going below zero.

items.title: EVE corporation and alliance logos share one component, and every EVE image address comes from one place
items.where_users_meet_it: Corporation and alliance logos beside a character's name on character sheets: the signed-in home board (/?character=<id>), the demo board (/?demo=full&character=9900000002) and a member's sheet in the industry workspace (/industry, after opening a member). The corporation avatar on corp cards in Industry Jobs (/industry/jobs). Corporation badges on the maps list in Atlas (/atlas). Corporation rows in a map's access editor (the Access dialog on a map). Character portraits in the map block list and access editor. Item and blueprint icons everywhere TypeIcon is used (see P009).
items.before: When images load normally, logos and portraits look exactly the same before and after this change. The differences are in two other situations. 1. A logo fails to load. On a character sheet, the 20px corporation or alliance logo disappeared completely, and the name slid left into the empty space. In the map access editor, the 32px corporation box was a broken that the browser drew in its own way, which could include a small broken-image icon. On the corp jobs card and the Atlas badges, the browser left an empty box. 2. A screen reader reads the sheet. Each logo was announced as "Federation Navy logo", followed by the name itself, so the corporation was heard twice. An unnamed corporation was announced as "Corporation logo". In code, each screen built its own image-server address: the board logo, the item icons, and three hand-made corporation-logo images in Corp Jobs, the Atlas catalogue and the access editor.
items.after:
With images loading normally, there is no visible change. Every picture is fetched from exactly the same address as before, because the image loader always rewrites the size. Stored portrait links still end in size=128.

When a logo fails to load, every screen now leaves an empty box of the same size, and the same border where the screen has one. Nothing shifts. On a character sheet this means a blank 20px gap before "Federation Navy" or "Halcyon Drift" (about 26px including the spacing), where the name used to slide left. In the access editor, the broken-image placeholder becomes a clean, empty bordered square.

Screen readers no longer announce logos beside a name, so the corporation or alliance name is read once. The access editor still labels its corporation logo with the corporation name while the logo loads.
items.behind_the_scenes: src/lib/eve-image.ts gains eveImageSrc(family, id, size), one builder with a path table for all seven image families. characterPortraitUrl now calls it, and corporationLogoUrl and eve-sso's portraitUrl are deleted. EntityLogo moves from components/composition/board/sections to src/components/entity-logo.tsx, as the logo counterpart of CharacterPortrait: typed sizes 20, 24, 32 and 36, alt defaults to '', and a failed logo leaves a same-size aria-hidden span. CorpJobsBoard, MapCatalogue and AccessListEditor now use it. Also removed: a never-set logoUrl field on map access options, and the redundant portrait src props in MapBlockList and AccessListEditor, since CharacterPortrait builds that URL itself. TypeIcon's src goes through eveImageSrc.
items.risk_notes:
Low risk. The review found every final image URL byte-identical: the loader rewrites ?size=, and stored portrait URLs keep size=128.

One design call for the owner. When a logo fails on a character sheet, a blank 20px slot now stays in place of the old collapse. The wave guide flagged this as "confirm with design, or keep returning null for 20px only".

The change only shows when an image fails. images.evetech.net is reachable from the sandbox, and even the demo board's fake alliance id (99900000001) returns a default logo with HTTP 200. So the shot has to block images.evetech.net in the browser.

The Corp Jobs avatar, Atlas corp badges and access-editor corp rows can't be shown locally. The E2E Pilot has no corporation and no ESI tokens, so only live EVE data shows them. The demo board's sheet header is the representative shot.

Logos that load normally need no shot: nothing changes there.

items.title: Item icon fallback letters use real initials, and the 30px icon fallback is really 30px
items.where_users_meet_it:
Only when an item, blueprint or ship picture fails to load from the EVE image server. Places it shows:
- Blueprint pages /industry/<blueprintId>: the big 112px blueprint tile, the build-plan node icons, the Raw ledger rows, and the component drawer.
- The planner search and its Recents/Favorites shelves at /industry/planner.
- Item and blueprint results in the site search in the header.
- Industry job rows at /industry/jobs.
- The ship icon on a character sheet (board and workspace).
- Structure hull tiles in the Structures drawer (/industry?panel=structures).
items.before:
When an item picture failed, the tile showed two letters, usually the first two letters of the whole name: "Heavy Water" showed HE and "Damage Control II" showed DA. Industry job rows were the exception, since they already used initials (HW), so the same item could read differently on different screens.

Names with odd starts gave odd letters: "R.A.M.- Armor/Hull Tech" showed R., and a quoted name like "'Moreau' Fortizar" showed 'M or 'F.

In the planner, the 30px icons (build-plan nodes and the Raw ledger) fell back to a 32px tile. In the Raw ledger, whose icon column is exactly 30px, the failed tile poked 2px past its column.
items.after:
The fallback shows the first letter of each of the first two words, the same rule on every screen. For example:
- Heavy Water HW
- Damage Control II DC
- Oscillator Capacitor Unit OC
- Mechanical Parts MP
- Liquid Ozone LO
- Helium Isotopes HI
- R.A.M.- Armor/Hull Tech RA
- 'Moreau' Fortizar MF (quote marks are skipped)

Single-word names are unchanged (Tritanium TR, Morphite MO), and so are short labels such as BP, C3, Ra or the → arrow. An empty name still shows ?.

The 30px fallback tile is now exactly 30px, so it fits the Raw ledger column and is 2px smaller inside the build-plan node frame. All other fallback sizes are pixel-identical: 22, 26, 32, 40, 64 and 112.

When the picture loads normally, nothing changes.
items.behind_the_scenes: TypeIcon's fallback text is now initials(mono || alt) || '?'. The ten call sites that passed name.slice(0, 2) now pass the full name. PlannerRail and ComponentDrawer drop mono and let alt feed it. JobRow no longer calls initials() itself. TypeIcon's size is a closed type, 22, 26, 30, 32, 40, 64 or 112, with a size-[30px] class added. The unused 88 is gone, and so is the silent 'unknown size means 32' default, so the compiler rejects unsupported sizes. initials() in lib/format/names.ts now starts each word at its first letter or digit.
items.risk_notes:
Low risk, and the change is visible only when an image fails: the image server has no picture for that type, or is down. Local shots need images.evetech.net blocked in the browser.

A judgment call for the owner. Single-word names followed by a Roman numeral now take the numeral as their second word: Hammerhead II reads HI (was HA), Warrior II reads WI (was WA). Digit-led names read like "125mm Gatling AutoCannon II" giving 1G (was 12). The wave declared this as intended.

The ship tile on a character sheet and the structure hull tiles change only for multi-word or quoted names. The demo board's ships are single words (Tengu, Ishtar and so on), and the E2E Pilot owns no structures, so those can't be shown locally. Blueprint 2049 (Damage Control II) has enough multi-word inputs to show the rule, and local SDE and market prices exist for it: 5,639 market_prices rows, and its tree and flat materials include Heavy Water. Reviewers found no defects in this lens.

items.after: There is one shared copy of the system list. When any screen loads it, every open screen fills in at once. That slip was never on staging, so compared with staging the composer shows a picked system at once, as it does today. The System suggestions and the exact-name match still use the full search hook, unchanged.

That is a handful of requests per 15 s per tab, all to a cached, public endpoint, which is cheap. Because the store renders with the server's empty value during hydration, it also removes a rare timing case: a late-hydrating panel could have disagreed with the server HTML if the list had already loaded. Both worktrees were created outside the repo with `git worktree add --detach`. OLD is origin/staging at 17841eec ("Merge pull request #673") in p8/wt-old, served on http://localhost:3101. NEW is origin/development at 3a8e28c3 ("Fix promote review round 1") in p8/wt-new, served on http://localhost:3102. Each worktree got `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` (7s from the store; no symlink fallback needed) and a copy of .env.local, which was never printed. Each ran `pnpm exec next dev -p <port>` with DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED and DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL set to local Postgres :5433, CONVEX_AGENT_MODE=anonymous, SUPERADMIN_CHARACTER_ID=9000001, and BETTER_AUTH_URL, SITE_URL and AUTH_ISSUER_URL set to http://localhost:<port>. Logs are p8/dev-old.log and p8/dev-new.log. Both answered 200 on / straight away. There are no schema or convex/ differences between the two refs, so sharing the database and Convex was safe.

Auth deviation: POST /api/dev/synthetic-pilot returns 500 on both refs when SUPERADMIN_CHARACTER_ID=9000001. The guard in synthetic-pilot-store.ts throws "The synthetic pilot cannot be the configured superadmin". So I minted the pilot once with `pnpm e2e:seed --out=p8/auth.json`, run from wt-new with SUPERADMIN unset, as .env.local has it. Both servers then used the resulting better-auth.session_token cookie (domain localhost, so it works on both ports). Because the servers run with SUPERADMIN=9000001, that one session is the E2E Pilot and is also admin. I confirmed /admin/traffic returned 200 on both. This reset the E2E Pilot once, which revokes any earlier pilot session, including one on :3000.

Convex logged "No auth provider found" errors in the console on 3101/3102 because its issuer is localhost:3000. None of the shots depend on Convex auth.

pairs.problem: Minor: the crop cuts the '← All characters' link at the top edge. The tighter row-only crops (p008-board-logos-failed-before-row.png / -after-row.png) show the same shift more clearly and can be used instead.

pairs.name: p009-planner-blueprint-monograms
pairs.caption: Build plan with icons blocked, so letter tiles show instead. Before: the first two letters (big tile 'DA', 'OS', 'QU', 'HE' for Heavy Water). After: initials ('DC' for Damage Control II, 'OC', 'QM', 'HW'), which tell similar names apart. Single-word items like Oxygen stay 'OX'.

pairs.name: p009-raw-ledger-monograms
pairs.caption: Raw ledger with icons blocked. Before: tiles show the first two letters, so Heavy Water and Helium Isotopes both read 'HE'. After: initials ('HW', 'HI', 'LO', 'OI', 'ED', 'MP', 'CB'). One-word materials (Tritanium, Pyerite, Morphite) are unchanged.
pairs.problem: The 2px tile-size fix (32px to 30px) is not visible at this scale; only the letter change can be judged.

pairs.name: p009-blueprint-search-monograms
pairs.caption: Blueprint search for 'Damage Control', icons blocked. Before: tiles read DA, DA, CI, AS, 'R, AS (with a stray quote mark). After: DC, DC, CD, AD, RD, AD, one letter per word, with the quote dropped.

pairs.name: p003-board-skeleton-lg
pairs.caption: Loading placeholder of the home board on a laptop-width screen. Before: a big top circle and 64px pilot circles, with the cards starting further left. After: all circles are smaller (56px) and the left column is wider, matching the real board so the page doesn't jump when it loads.

pairs.name: p003-board-skeleton-xl
pairs.caption: Same loading placeholder on a wide screen. The circles are the same on both. Only the left column is wider on After, so the grey card blocks start about 32px further right, matching the loaded board.

pairs.name: p003-add-character-focus
pairs.caption: 'Add character' button reached with the keyboard. Before: focus ring only, with grey '+' and grey text. After: the same ring, and the '+' and label turn green, as they already do on mouse hover.
pairs.problem: The plan said 'gold', but the colour is green, and green is correct: the button uses the same text-isk (#3dd68c) for both hover and focus-visible. Describe it as green in the write-up.

pairs.name: p010-found-structure-security-colour
pairs.caption: Structure search results. Names and order are identical. Before: the security numbers are grey like the rest of the line. After: they are coloured by security, 0.4 orange (low-sec) and 0.9 blue (high-sec).

pairs.name: p010-secpill-unknown-security
pairs.caption: System field when a system's security is unknown. Before: the dash pill is red, which looks like null-sec. After: the pill is neutral grey, meaning unknown.

pairs.name: p010-structures-row-retry
pairs.caption: Saved structure after the system list failed once and then came back. Before: the row stays stuck on 'Raitaru' with no bonuses until a reload. After: it retries by itself and recovers to 'Raitaru · Amamake 0.4' with the bonus figures (-1.0%, -15.0%, cost -3.0%).

pairs.name: p005-primitives-action-form
pairs.caption: Preview page, Actions section. After adds two new specimen cards between Button and CopyButton: ActionForm ('Post back' plus a dimmed 'Unavailable') and ConfirmActionForm (a red 'Ask first'). Everything else is unchanged.

pairs.name: p012-admin-linked-characters
pairs.caption: Admin user page, Linked characters card. Identical on both, as expected locally. This orange chip slot is where the new 'Verification delayed' label will appear for a stuck character on staging and production.

pairs.name: p271-industry-head
pairs.caption: Link-preview tags for /industry. Before: an old Jita-rates description, the wide logo.png image, and a Twitter title of just 'LGI.tools'. After: 'Industry Planner' everywhere, the current workspace description, a site name tag, and the standard 1200x630 share card.

pairs.name: p271-industry-jobs-head
pairs.caption: Link-preview tags for /industry/jobs. Before: it borrows the home page's preview (title 'LGI.tools', the wormhole description, link pointing at the home page). After: its own title 'Active Jobs — Industry Planner', its own description and the correct link.
pairs.problem: Not in the plan: NEW drops the twitter:image:alt/type/width/height tags that OLD inherited, and the image alt text shortens to 'LGI.tools'. This is harmless for unfurling but worth one line in the write-up.

pairs.name: p271-industry-blueprint-head
pairs.caption: Link-preview tags for a blueprint page (Rifter). Title, description, link and breadcrumbs are the same. Only the image changes, from logo.png to the standard 1200x630 share card with size and alt text, plus a new site name tag.

pairs.name: p271-industry-share-card
pairs.caption: The picture Discord or X shows for an industry link. Before: the wide 'LO-GANG INDUSTRIES.TOOLS' logo (2400x1202, the wrong shape for a preview). After: the standard 1200x630 black card '[ LGI.tools ] EVE ONLINE TOOLS'.

pairs.name: p271-site-detail-head
pairs.caption: Link-preview tags for a wormhole site page. The only change is one new tag, og:site_name 'LGI.tools'. The site's own generated preview image is unchanged.

pairs.name: p271-unknown-blueprint-head
pairs.caption: A blueprint ID that doesn't exist, as fetched by a link-preview bot. Before: 200 OK with the home page's preview tags, and the noindex tag only arrives late. After: a real 404 with noindex at the top of the page. In a normal browser, both still return 200.
pairs.problem: The capture is sound and needs no re-shoot, but the plan's claim 'no home-page og:url' is wrong. On NEW the 404 still carries the home page's og:url (https://lgi.tools), title 'LGI.tools', generic description and root image, because the not-found page inherits the root layout's metadata. The code change is generateMetadata calling notFound() instead of returning {}. Fix the write-up to say 'now 404 with noindex first; preview tags are still the generic home ones'. Bots generally do not unfurl 404s.
